text: Tell me about a time when you had to work with a difficult team member. How did you handle the situation?

rubric.situation: Describe the team context and the difficult behavior
rubric.task: What was your role and responsibility in the situation
rubric.action: Specific steps taken to address the issue
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned

followUpPrompts: What specific actions did you take to improve the working relationship?
How did you ensure the team's goals weren't compromised?
What would you do differently if faced with a similar situation again?

text: Describe a situation where you had a conflict with a colleague or manager. How did you resolve it?

rubric.situation: Context of the disagreement or conflict
rubric.task: Your role and what was at stake
rubric.action: How you approached the conflict and communicated
rubric.result: Resolution and impact on the relationship

followUpPrompts: What was the root cause of the disagreement?
How did you balance your perspective with theirs?
What did this experience teach you about handling disagreements?

text: Give me an example of a time when you took initiative to lead a project or task without being asked.

rubric.situation: The context that needed leadership
rubric.task: What needed to be done and why no one else was doing it
rubric.action: How you stepped up and organized the work
rubric.result: Outcome and how others responded

followUpPrompts: How did you get buy-in from others to follow your lead?
What challenges did you face in taking ownership?
How did this experience shape your approach to leadership?

text: Tell me about a time when you failed at something important. What happened and what did you learn?

rubric.situation: The context and what you were trying to achieve
rubric.task: Your responsibility and what went wrong
rubric.action: How you responded to the failure
rubric.result: What you learned and how you applied it

followUpPrompts: What was the immediate impact of the failure?
How did you take accountability for what happened?
What specific changes did you make based on this experience?

text: Describe a complex problem you solved at work. Walk me through your approach.

rubric.situation: The problem context and constraints
rubric.task: What needed to be solved and why it was complex
rubric.action: Your systematic approach to solving it
rubric.result: The solution and its impact

followUpPrompts: What alternatives did you consider before settling on your approach?
How did you validate that your solution was correct?
What would you do differently if you encountered a similar problem again?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to work under tight deadlines or high pressure. How did you manage?

rubric.situation: The high-pressure context and constraints
rubric.task: What needed to be done and the stakes involved
rubric.action: How you prioritized and managed your work
rubric.result: Outcome and how you handled the stress

followUpPrompts: How did you decide what to prioritize when time was limited?
What strategies did you use to stay focused and productive?
How did this experience affect your approach to deadlines going forward?

text: Give me an example of a new skill or technology you had to learn quickly. How did you approach it?

rubric.situation: Why you needed to learn something new
rubric.task: What you needed to learn and the timeline
rubric.action: Your learning strategy and resources
rubric.result: How quickly you became proficient and applied it

followUpPrompts: What resources or methods were most effective for your learning?
How did you know when you had learned enough to apply it?
What would you do differently when learning something new in the future?

text: Describe a time when you had to explain a complex technical concept to a non-technical person.

rubric.situation: The context and who you were communicating with
rubric.task: What needed to be explained and why it mattered
rubric.action: How you adapted your communication style
rubric.result: Whether they understood and the outcome

followUpPrompts: How did you gauge whether they understood your explanation?
What analogies or examples did you use to make it clearer?
How did this experience change how you communicate technical ideas?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to collaborate with people from different departments or backgrounds.

rubric.situation: The cross-functional context
rubric.task: The shared goal and different perspectives involved
rubric.action: How you bridged gaps and aligned the team
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about collaboration

followUpPrompts: What challenges arose from the different perspectives?
How did you ensure everyone's voice was heard?
What made this collaboration successful or unsuccessful?

text: Describe a situation where you disagreed with a decision made by your team or manager. What did you do?

rubric.situation: The decision and why you disagreed
rubric.task: Your role and what was at stake
rubric.action: How you expressed your concerns
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned

followUpPrompts: How did you balance speaking up with respecting the decision?
What was the impact of your input on the final outcome?
How did this affect your relationship with the decision-maker?

text: Give me an example of when you mentored or helped a colleague grow in their role.

rubric.situation: The context and your colleague's needs
rubric.task: What you took on and why
rubric.action: How you supported their development
rubric.result: Their growth and what you learned

followUpPrompts: How did you identify what they needed help with?
What approach did you take to guide them without taking over?
How did this experience influence your view on mentorship?

text: Tell me about a time when you made a mistake that affected your team or project. How did you handle it?

rubric.situation: The context and what you were working on
rubric.task: Your responsibility and what went wrong
rubric.action: How you responded and communicated the issue
rubric.result: How you fixed it and what you learned

followUpPrompts: How soon did you realize there was a problem?
How did you communicate the mistake to others?
What systems or processes did you put in place to prevent it from happening again?

text: Describe a time when you identified an inefficiency in a process and improved it.

rubric.situation: The process and its problems
rubric.task: What you noticed and why it mattered
rubric.action: How you analyzed and redesigned the process
rubric.result: The improvement and its measurable impact

followUpPrompts: How did you measure the improvement?
What resistance did you face and how did you overcome it?
What did this teach you about process optimization?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to juggle multiple priorities with competing deadlines.

rubric.situation: The competing priorities and constraints
rubric.task: What needed to be done and the stakes
rubric.action: How you prioritized and managed your time
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about prioritization

followUpPrompts: How did you decide which tasks to focus on first?
Did you have to delegate or say no to anything? How did you handle that?
What strategies did you use to stay organized under pressure?

text: Give me an example of a time when you received constructive criticism. How did you respond?

rubric.situation: The context and who gave the feedback
rubric.task: What the feedback was about
rubric.action: How you processed and acted on it
rubric.result: What you changed and the outcome

followUpPrompts: What was your initial reaction to the feedback?
How did you decide which parts to act on?
How has this feedback changed your work since then?

text: Describe a situation where you had to persuade others to adopt your idea or approach.

rubric.situation: The context and resistance you faced
rubric.task: What you were trying to convince others of
rubric.action: How you built your case and addressed concerns
rubric.result: Whether you succeeded and what you learned

followUpPrompts: What was the main objection you had to overcome?
How did you tailor your message to different stakeholders?
What would you do differently if you had to persuade someone again?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to adapt to a significant change at work.

rubric.situation: The change and its impact
rubric.task: What you needed to adapt to
rubric.action: How you approached the change
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about adaptability

followUpPrompts: What was most challenging about the change?
How did you stay motivated during the transition?
What did this experience teach you about handling change?

text: Describe a time when you went above and beyond what was expected of you.

rubric.situation: The context and what was expected
rubric.task: What you chose to do beyond that
rubric.action: The extra effort you put in
rubric.result: The impact and how it was received

followUpPrompts: What motivated you to go the extra mile?
How did you balance this with your other responsibilities?
What did this experience teach you about setting standards?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to adapt your communication style for a stakeholder with very different expectations or priorities.

rubric.situation: The stakeholder context and differing expectations
rubric.task: What you needed to achieve and why alignment mattered
rubric.action: How you adapted your approach to bridge the gap
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about stakeholder management

followUpPrompts: How did you identify what mattered most to that stakeholder?
What would you do differently if the relationship was hostile?
How has this experience shaped your approach to managing up?

text: Describe a situation where you identified a risk or potential problem before it became critical. What did you do?

rubric.situation: The context and early warning signs you noticed
rubric.task: Why the risk mattered and what could have gone wrong
rubric.action: How you communicated the risk and what steps you took
rubric.result: Outcome and whether your intervention was appreciated

followUpPrompts: How did you build confidence to speak up about something uncertain?
What framework do you use to assess risks vs. rewards?
Has this experience changed how you approach risk assessment?

text: Give me an example of when you had to own a mistake publicly in front of your team or stakeholders. How did you handle it?

rubric.situation: The context and what went wrong
rubric.task: Your responsibility and the impact of the mistake
rubric.action: How you communicated the mistake and what you did to fix it
rubric.result: How the team responded and what you learned about accountability

followUpPrompts: How did you rebuild trust after the mistake?
What systems did you put in place to prevent recurrence?
How has this experience shaped your approach to transparency?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to make a decision with incomplete information. What was your approach?

rubric.situation: The context and why information was incomplete
rubric.task: What decision needed to be made and the stakes involved
rubric.action: How you gathered what you could and made the best choice
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about decision-making under uncertainty

followUpPrompts: How did you know when you had enough information to decide?
What would you have done differently with more time?
How did you communicate the uncertainty to stakeholders?

text: Describe a time when you proactively improved a team process or workflow without being asked to do so.

rubric.situation: The team context and the inefficiency you noticed
rubric.task: Why you felt ownership over the problem
rubric.action: How you designed the improvement and got buy-in
rubric.result: The impact on team productivity or morale

followUpPrompts: How did you get the team to adopt the change?
What resistance did you face and how did you overcome it?
How did you measure the improvement's impact?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to say no to a request from a senior leader or important stakeholder. How did you handle it?

rubric.situation: The request and why it was problematic
rubric.task: Your responsibility and what was at stake
rubric.action: How you communicated your position respectfully
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about managing expectations

followUpPrompts: How did you prepare for that conversation?
What alternatives did you offer instead of a flat refusal?
How did this experience affect your confidence in similar situations?

text: Tell me about a time when project requirements changed significantly midway through. How did you adapt your approach?

rubric.situation: The project context and what changed
rubric.task: Your role and what needed to be adjusted
rubric.action: How you adapted your plan, priorities, and communication
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about flexibility

followUpPrompts: How did you communicate the changes to your team and stakeholders?
What was the hardest part of shifting direction?
How did this experience change how you plan projects going forward?

text: Describe a time when you had to learn a completely new technology or framework under a tight deadline. How did you approach it?

rubric.situation: Why you needed to learn the new technology
rubric.task: What you needed to build and the timeline
rubric.action: Your learning strategy and how you applied it
rubric.result: What you delivered and how proficient you became

followUpPrompts: What resources were most effective in your learning process?
How did you balance learning with delivering on time?
What would you do differently when facing a similar learning curve?

text: Give me an example of how you managed your time when you had multiple important tasks competing for your attention.

rubric.situation: The competing tasks and why they were all important
rubric.task: Your responsibility for each task
rubric.action: How you prioritized, scheduled, and executed
rubric.result: Outcome for each task and what you learned

followUpPrompts: How did you decide which task to tackle first?
Did you have to delegate or push back on any deadlines?
What tools or techniques helped you stay organized?

text: Tell me about a time when you realized you could not meet a deadline. What did you do?

rubric.situation: The project and why the deadline was at risk
rubric.task: Your responsibility and what was expected
rubric.action: How you communicated early and what trade-offs you proposed
rubric.result: Outcome and what you learned about estimation

followUpPrompts: How soon did you raise the flag about the deadline risk?
What alternatives did you propose to the stakeholder?
How did this experience change how you estimate tasks?

text: Describe a time when you mentored a junior team member through a challenging technical problem.

rubric.situation: The junior member and the challenge they faced
rubric.task: Your role as mentor and what they needed
rubric.action: How you guided them without solving it for them
rubric.result: Their growth and what you learned about teaching

followUpPrompts: How did you balance guiding them with letting them figure it out?
What signs told you they were starting to understand?
How has this experience shaped your mentoring approach?

text: Tell me about a time when you had to make a technical decision that affected other teams or stakeholders. How did you handle the cross-team communication?

rubric.situation: The decision and which teams were affected
rubric.task: Your responsibility and what was at stake
rubric.action: How you gathered input, communicated the decision, and handled concerns
rubric.result: Outcome and how cross-team relationships were affected

followUpPrompts: How did you ensure all affected teams had a voice in the decision?
What pushback did you receive and how did you address it?
How did you document and share the rationale with the wider organization?

text: Give me an example of a time when you took full ownership of a project from start to finish without direct supervision.

rubric.situation: The project and why you owned it
rubric.task: What you were responsible for delivering
rubric.action: How you planned, executed, and communicated progress
rubric.result: What you delivered and how it was received

followUpPrompts: How did you keep yourself accountable without a manager checking in?
What was the biggest challenge of working independently?
How did this experience affect how you handle ownership going forward?
